summary: Both render the same subject — a blue-cored candle flame over a blue base glow on a near-black field with sparse sparkles — but the port's flame barely flickers and its blue base glow is ~4x too tall and bright, flipping the image from warm-dominant to blue-dominant and washing the flame's gold lower half to pale pink.
observations: Both sides alive, no compile or runtime errors, single steady regime with no mode rotation and no decay: a 240 s / 2 fps survey rhythm image is uniform end-to-end on both sides, and a --skip 120 --seconds 12 late window looks identical to t=0 (orig brightnessTrend steady, port steady, zeroMotionFrames 0 on both).

Overall colour balance is inverted. Default 16x16 rig, 240 s survey: orig meanR/G/B = 39.2 / 19.3 / 20.0 (warm-dominant, roughly 2:1:1); port = 28.6 / 11.4 / 33.3 (blue-dominant). Mean brightness is close (orig 26.2, port 24.4), so this is hue distribution, not level.

Blue base glow is ~4x too tall on the port. --dump at 48x48, far-left column outside the flame: orig's base occupies rows 43-47 of 48 (bottom ~10% of the panel), port's occupies rows 29-47 (bottom ~40%). On the default 16x16 rig orig's base is exactly rows 14-15 (area ~24 px, x-ramp 14,31,48,65,82,99 symmetric about centre, peak B=99 rock steady across 16 sampled times); port's is rows ~9-15 (area ~63 px, ramp 12,38,63,89,114,140, peak B pulsing 146-167).

That oversized base is additively blended OVER the flame instead of sitting below it. Orig's warm ring keeps B=0 all the way down (row 8 = 224,106,0; row 10 = 228,135,0; row 12 = 215,152,0 — red at the tip ramping to gold/amber at the base). Port's ring picks up the base's blue from row 9 down (row 9 = 229,107,89; row 11 = 229,130,114; row 12 = 229,142,140), so the flame's bottom half reads as pale pink/white rather than gold. The R,G part of the warm ramp is otherwise comparable between sides (both peak at R=229).

Flame flicker is essentially missing on the port. 48x48, per-row left/right edges of the lit silhouette over t=1.00-1.60 (0.2 s steps): orig's row-8 edges swing 14-18 / 29-33 and rows 12/16/20 move 1-3 px each sample — the flame visibly sways and bulges; port's silhouette is bit-identical below row 12 across the whole 0.6 s and moves at most 1 px at the tip. The filmstrips show the same thing: orig's outline reshapes every frame, port's is a rigid ellipse that only breathes slightly.

Motion stat backs it up: survey (60 s/5 fps) orig motion avg 4.6 max 9 vs port 1.8 max 3; 240 s survey orig 5 vs port 2; late 12 s window at 20 fps orig avg 1.7 max 5 vs port avg 1.0 with min = max = 1 (literally invariant).

Blue core texture differs. Orig's core is mottled with ridges running diagonally — blue-channel values inside it swing 100-252 with multiple separate peaks per row (48x48 rows 22-30, peaks wandering across cols 21-27), which reads as diagonal striping in the render. Port's core is one smooth blob with a solid clipped 255 plateau (cols ~21-24, rows ~22-28) and a clean falloff — no striping.
Core hue differs slightly: orig's brightest core pixels have G > R (e.g. 44,67,224 / 47,71,239 — cyan-leaning blue); port's have R > G (86,62,255 / 81,58,255 — violet-leaning blue).

Flame footprint is ~25% smaller and narrower on the port. Default 16x16, warm pixels (R>60) averaged over 16 sampled times: orig ~55 px spanning cols 4-11, port ~42 px spanning cols 5-10. Vertical extent is similar (rows ~2-13 both).

Both sides emit sparse sparkles in the dark field, but they differ in colour and rate: orig's are near-neutral white (peak samples 189,165,161 / 145,126,123), port's are warm gold (152,129,99 / 141,120,91). Counting lit pixels in the outer columns (x<2 or x>13) over 16 sampled frames: orig ~0.4/frame, port ~1.1/frame — port sparkles roughly 2x as often (small sample; the 240 s rhythm images and the late-window sheets show the same imbalance).
Background is effectively identical: orig (2,0,5), port (2,0,3).
Control surface matches: --probe-controls reports 'no settable controls' on BOTH sides, and meta.json lists controls: [] for each. No dial work possible or needed.

Both sides are resolution-independent in the same way — re-rendered at 48x48 each draws the same picture at finer detail (same proportions, same feature count), so the divergences above are not a rig artefact. All headline numbers were confirmed on the default 16x16 grid rig.
Seed-independent: --seed 7 over 20 s at 10 fps reproduces the same per-side statistics (orig meanR/G/B 39.3/19.4/20.0 motion 2.9; port 28.6/11.4/33.3 motion 1.5).
feedback: Shrink the blue base glow. On a 16-row grid the original's glow covers only the bottom 2 rows (bottom ~10% of the panel at any resolution — confirmed rows 43-47 of 48 at 48x48); the port covers the bottom ~40%. Cut its vertical extent to about a quarter of what it is now.

Dim the base glow and stop it pulsing. Original's centre-column peak blue is a steady 99/255 on the default rig, never varying across a 12 s window; the port's is 146-167 and breathes. Target a constant ~100 peak with the same symmetric left-to-right ramp (14,31,48,65,82,99 across the 12 lit columns).

Composite the base glow BEHIND/BELOW the flame, not added on top of it. In the original the warm ring has B=0 for its whole length, so the flame goes red at the tip -> orange -> gold/amber at the base (row 12 is 215,152,0). In the port the glow's blue is summed into the ring from row 9 down, producing 229,142,140 pale pink where gold belongs. Fixing the extent alone will not fix this — the ring's blue channel must stay at 0 wherever the flame is drawn.

Restore the flame's flicker — this is the biggest behavioural gap and the defining feature of a candle. The original's outline sways and reshapes continuously: its left/right edges in the upper half move 2-3 px (on a 48-wide grid) between samples 0.2 s apart, and its motion stat averages 4.6 over a 60 s survey. The port's outline is frozen below the upper third and its motion stat sits pinned at exactly 1. Add per-frame noise-driven distortion to the flame silhouette, strongest near the tip and tapering to nothing at the base (the original's bottom rows barely move either).

Give the blue core its internal texture back. The original's core is not a solid fill: its brightness varies 100-252 within the core with several bright ridges running diagonally (lower-left to upper-right), clearly visible as stripes at 48x48. The port's core is a flat clipped 255 blob — reduce the peak so it stops saturating and modulate it with the missing diagonal texture.
Widen the flame slightly. Original's warm ring spans 8 of 16 columns (cols 4-11, ~55 lit px); port's spans 6 (cols 5-10, ~42 px) — about 25% too small in area.
Cool the sparkles and thin them out. Original's sparkles are near-white (R:G:B about 1.00:0.87:0.85); the port's are distinctly gold (about 1.00:0.85:0.65) and appear roughly twice as often.
Nudge the core hue: original's brightest core pixels have green above red (44,67,224), the port's have red above green (86,62,255) — the port's blue core is a shade too violet.
